**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2022/05/05 (Thu) 23:53
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Electronic Performance Support Systems (EPSS) are computer-based systems that provide on-the-job support to workers, enabling them to perform their tasks more efficiently and effectively.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS can be used in a variety of settings, including education and training, to support learning and performance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS are designed to provide just-in-time support to users, allowing them to access the information and tools they need to complete their tasks quickly and effectively.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS can include access to instructional materials, reference guides, job aids, and other resources.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS can be accessed through a variety of devices, including desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones, making them highly flexible and portable.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS have the potential to significantly improve performance and productivity in a variety of settings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] By providing just-in-time support, EPSS can help users overcome barriers to learning and performance, and reduce the time and effort required to complete tasks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EPSS can also help to improve the quality of work by providing access to accurate and up-to-date information and resources.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The success of EPSS implementation depends on the acceptance and use of these systems by the individuals who will be using them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Factors such as perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and user attitudes can all influence the acceptance and use of EPSS.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Research has shown that the role of instructional designers in the design and implementation of EPSS is critical.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Competencies such as knowledge of the learner, the learning environment, and the learning objectives are important for instructional designers to possess in order to effectively design and implement EPSS.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] According to the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use are key determinants of user acceptance (Davis, 1989).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Davis et al. (1989) found that both perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were significantly related to user acceptance of computer technology.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mathieson (1991) found that the TAM was a good predictor of user intentions to use technology.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ashraf et al. (2017) found that interfunctional communication was an important factor in the acceptance of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems.
